output: You're right to worry about that, and model building does have a learning curve. Most non-finance users shouldn't start by designing models. They should start by entering and reviewing numbers in input views set up for their role, so clinic managers can focus on their own staffing figures without working in the model's structure. Onboarding also includes admin training, and a trained internal admin handles routine model changes, so those changes don't need to go through a consultant. [PROOF] Would it help to set up a hands-on session where two of your non-finance budget owners complete a real input task in a sandbox? That would show you how a clinic manager would actually work before anything goes live.

messages.content:
<quote>
My worry is that our clinic managers aren't spreadsheet people, and if they can't update their own staffing numbers this ends up back on my desk.
</quote>
